# Wantastic — Console User Guide

## What is Wantastic?

Wantastic is a private overlay network service.  It lets you connect your
devices securely and access them from anywhere through a web console.

The console is at **https://console.wantastic.app**.

---

## Getting Started

### 1. Get an account

Wantastic is admin-provisioned — there is no public sign-up. Ask your
administrator to create an account for you. They'll send you an email
and an initial password.

1. Open the console URL provided by your administrator.
2. Log in with the credentials they sent you.
3. You are taken straight to the dashboard.

### 2. Download the agent

1. In the console, click **Add Device** (top-right of the Devices page).
2. Select your operating system from the dropdown (Linux, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android).
3. Click **Download Agent** and run the installer on your device.

### 3. Connect a device

After the agent is installed and running on your device:

1. The agent displays a URL, for example:
   ```
   Open this URL to log in: https://console.wantastic.app/activate?user_code=ABCD-1234
   ```
2. Open that URL in any browser.
3. Log in with your account — Google, GitHub, or email/password (whichever you set up).
4. After you approve, the agent connects automatically.
5. The device appears in your **Devices** list within a few seconds, shown as
   **Online** with its assigned private IP address.

The login page is hosted by Auth0 — no separate portal page exists for this step.
No manual configuration is needed — the device is now part of your private network.

---

## Devices Page

The **Devices** page (`/devices`) is the main view of your network.

Each device card shows:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| Name | The hostname of the device (editable — click the pencil icon). |
| Status | Green dot = online and reachable.  Grey = offline. |
| Private IP | The IP address other devices use to reach this device. |
| Last Seen | When the device last checked in. |
| Platform | The operating system of the device. |

**Actions available on each device:**

- **Rename** — click the pencil icon next to the device name and type a new name.
- **SSH** — opens a browser terminal directly to the device (Linux only, device must be online).
- **Open** — opens a browser proxy to an HTTP/HTTPS service on the device (enter the port number when prompted).
- **WinBox** — opens the MikroTik WinBox interface in the browser (MikroTik devices only).
- **Remove** — permanently removes the device from your network.  The device goes offline immediately.

---

## Groups Page

Groups (`/groups`) let you organise devices so you can apply access rules to
many devices at once.

**Create a group:**

1. Click **New Group**.
2. Enter a name (e.g. "Servers", "Laptops", "IoT").
3. Click **Save**.

**Add a device to a group:**

1. Open the device from the Devices page.
2. In the **Groups** section of the device detail panel, click **Add to Group**.
3. Select the group from the list and click **Confirm**.

A device can belong to multiple groups.

---

## Access Rules Page

Access rules (`/access`) control which devices can connect to each other.

By default, every device in your account can reach every other device.  Use
rules to restrict that.

**Add a deny rule:**

1. Click **New Rule**.
2. Under **Source**, select a group (or a single device).
3. Under **Destination**, select another group (or device).
4. Set the action to **Deny**.
5. Click **Save Rule**.

Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom.  The first matching rule wins.  Drag rules
to reorder them.

**Example — block IoT devices from reaching Servers:**

1. Create a group called "IoT" and a group called "Servers".
2. Add relevant devices to each group.
3. Create a Deny rule: Source = IoT → Destination = Servers.

IoT devices can no longer initiate connections to any device in the Servers group.

---

## Web SSH

Web SSH lets you open a terminal to any online Linux device directly in your
browser — no SSH client, no open ports, no VPN setup beyond Wantastic.

1. Go to **Devices**, find the device you want to access.
2. Click the **SSH** button.
3. A terminal window opens in the browser.
4. Log in with your device credentials as normal.

> The device must be online and have an SSH server running.

---

## Web Proxy

Web Proxy lets you access any HTTP or HTTPS service running on a device
through a secure browser tunnel.

1. Go to **Devices**, find the device.
2. Click **Open**.
3. Enter the port number of the service (e.g. `8080` for a web app, `443` for HTTPS).
4. Click **Connect**.
5. The service opens in a new browser tab proxied through the console.

Useful for admin panels, dashboards, or internal tools that are not exposed to
the internet.

---

## MikroTik / WinBox

If a device is a MikroTik router connected to your network:

1. Go to **Devices** and find the MikroTik router.
2. Click **WinBox**.
3. Enter the MikroTik admin username and password when prompted.
4. The WinBox management interface opens in the browser.

No WinBox desktop application or direct network access to the router is needed.

---

## Account Limits

Each tenant has a per-account device cap (`max_peers`) set by the super-admin.
There is no public sign-up and no billing — accounts are provisioned by an
admin who specifies the device limit at creation time.

If you need a higher cap, ask your administrator to raise it.

---

## Notifications

1. Go to **Settings → Notifications**.
2. Click **Add Notification**.
3. Choose the event type:
   - **Device Online** / **Device Offline** — alerts when a device connects or disconnects.
4. Choose the delivery channel:
   - **Email** — enters your email address.
   - **Webhook** — enter a URL; the console will POST a JSON payload to it.
5. Click **Save**.

To remove a notification, click the trash icon next to it.

---

## Account Settings

Go to **Settings** (top-right avatar menu) to manage your account.

- **Profile** — change your display name or email address, then click **Save**.
- **Security** — click **Enable 2FA**, scan the QR code with an authenticator
  app (e.g. Google Authenticator), and enter the 6-digit code to confirm.
- **Sessions** — lists every active login session with the browser and
  location.  Click **Revoke** on any session to sign it out remotely.
- **Danger Zone** — click **Delete Account** to permanently remove your
  account, all devices, and all data.  This action cannot be undone.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Do I need to open any ports on my firewall?**
No.  The agent establishes outbound connections only.  No inbound ports need
to be opened.

**Can I connect devices on different networks?**
Yes.  Devices on different ISPs, behind NAT, or in different countries all
appear on the same private network once activated.

**Is traffic encrypted?**
Yes.  All traffic between devices is end-to-end encrypted.
Wantastic never sees the content of your traffic.

**What happens if I exceed my device limit?**
New devices cannot be activated until your administrator raises the cap or
you remove existing devices.  Already-connected devices continue working normally.

**How do I remove a device permanently?**
Go to **Devices**, open the device, and click **Remove Device**.  This
immediately revokes the device's access to the network.

**Can I rename a device?**
Yes.  Click the pencil icon next to the device name on the Devices page.
